messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] merge multiple methyRawList objects or input large files
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
this memory consumption is higher than I would expect with methyl*DB objects, but it can be that it uses so much memory for the initial creation of the tabix files.
You could try to call the methRead function on each file separately, with the `dbtype = "tabix"` option set to create the tabix files. Then you can use the same tabix files for a new call to methRead using all the tabix files to create your methylRawListDB object and proceed with that.
This should work if your single file usage is in the range of 30GB from the 64GB.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: in package methylKit how to simultaneously use Rsamtools packages to deal with large dataset in desktop computer or laptop with limited RAM
messages.subject_clean: in package methylKit how to simultaneously use Rsamtools packages to deal with large dataset in desktop computer or laptop with limited RAM
messages.body_plain:
details as following:but i don't kown the how to realize it.
The methylKit package provides very similar capability by exploiting
flat file databases to substitute in-memory objects if the objects
grow too large. The internal data apart from meta information has a
tabular structure storing chromosome, start/end position, strand information
of the associated CpG base just like many other biological
formats like BED, GFF or SAM. By exporting this tabular data into a
TAB-delimited file and making sure it is accordingly position-sorted it
can be indexed using the generic Tabix tool (Lövkvist et al., 2016). In
general “Tabix indexing is a generalization of BAM indexing for generic
TAB-delimited files. It inherits all the advantages of BAM indexing,
including data compression and efficient random access in terms of few
seek function calls per query.” (Li, 2011). MethylKit relies on Rsamtools
(http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/Rsamtools.
html) which implements tabix functionality for R and this way
internal methylKit objects can be efficiently stored as compressed file
on the disk and still be fast accessed. Another advantage is that existing
compressed files can be loaded in interactive sessions, allowing the
backup and transfer of intermediate analysis results.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Alan, I have a similar problem to the one you encountered with your bed file and also realized that some of my chromosome IDs have underscores while others do not. I would like to delete the underscores and try the readTranscriptFeatures() again to. Please could you help provide me with the command you used to remove the underscores from your chromosome names? I know very little about scripts.

Many thanks

Relindis

On Saturday, September 1, 2018 at 4:13:43 AM UTC+2, Alan Hudson wrote:
> I think I have an answer to at least get readTranscriptFeatures() to recognize my BED files.
>
> I found that the chromosome names from the RefSeq gff3 file I am using, had an "_" as in "NC_XXXXX". By merely removing the underscore from the chromosome name and then converting the gff3 using gffToGenePred and genePredToBed, the resulting BED file now appears to work with readTranscriptFeatures()
>
>
> On Thursday, 30 August 2018 22:40:51 UTC-10, Alan Hudson wrote:
> > Hi,
> >
> > I have a similar problem and would appreciate some advice
> >
> > I am trying to use a RefSeq gff3 file to annotate DMRs with gene parts in methylKit. I have followed both suggested solutions in this thread but with limited success
> >
> > I have tried using gffToGenePred and genePredToBed, this produces a 12-column bed format file, however when I try to use readTranscriptFeatures() on the resulting bed file, I get:
> >
> > > Reading the table...
> > > Calculating intron coordinates...
> > > Error in rep(1:nrow(ref), ref[, 10]) : invalid 'times' argument
> >
> > I have also tried extracting the relevant gene feature coordinates using commands in the GenomicFeatures package. However, when the individual GRange objects for each individual gene part (TSS, intron, exon etc.) are combined they form a GenomicRangesList and when I use the command annotateWithGeneParts(), I get the following error message:
> >
> > > Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
> >   unable to find an inherited method for function ‘annotateWithGeneParts’ for signature ‘"GRanges", "SimpleGenomicRangesList"’
> >
> > Any advice on how to overcome either of these obstacles?
> >
> > Many thanks,
> >
> > Alan
> >
> > On Wednesday, 11 July 2018 04:21:09 UTC-10, Johan Zicola wrote:
> > > This reply is probably too late for Alejandro but it will save time for other plant scientists:
> > >
> > > Here the method for Arabidopsis thaliana. For other plant species, just look around in ftp://ftp.ensemblgenomes.org/pub/release-39/plants
> > > N.B: I assume you work on a Linux or Mac OS X machine.
> > > Download the gtf file Arabidopsis_thaliana.TAIR10.39.gtf.gz at ftp://ftp.ensemblgenomes.org/pub/release-39/plants/gtf/arabidopsis_thaliana/
> > > Check if chromosome names match with the nomenclature you use in your methylKit objects (for instance replace in the gtf file 1 by Chr1, 2 by Chr2, ... in vim by typing :%s/^\([1-9]\)/Chr\1/g  meaning 'add to all digits at beginning of lines the prefix "Chr"')
> > > Download from http://hgdownload.cse.ucsc.edu/admin/exe/linux.x86_64/ the two scripts gtfToGenePred and genePredToBed and put them in your ~/bin/ or wherever you keep your programs
> > > Uncompress your gtf file ($ gunzip Arabidopsis_thaliana.TAIR10.39.gtf.gz )
> > > Generate a genePred file ($ ~/bin/gtfToGenePred Arabidopsis_thaliana.TAIR10.39.gtf   Arabidopsis_thaliana.TAIR10.39.genePred )
> > > Generate a 12bed file ($ ~/bin/genePredToBed Arabidopsis_thaliana.TAIR10.39.genePred   Arabidopsis_thaliana.TAIR10.39.bed )
> > > Sort your bed file by chromosome and start position ($ sort -k 1,1 -k2,2n Arabidopsis_thaliana.TAIR10.39.bed -o Arabidopsis_thaliana.TAIR10.39.bed)
> > > Go in R and upload this bed file ( > readTranscriptFeatures("/path/to/Arabidopsis_thaliana.TAIR10.39.bed")
> > > Your gene.obj is now ready to be used as "feature" argument in annotateWithGeneParts or regionCounts.
> > >
> > > Best,
> > >
> > > Johan

messages.body_plain:
Hi Relindis,

I didn't use a script. I just went for the very basic method of opening the files in a text editor (BBEdit) and the using the find and replace functions to replace "_" with "". I did this for both the GFF3 annotation file and the DMR files - saving with a different name to avoid confusing the edited files with the original files.

I guess this method could cause errors but it seemed to work fine for me (and was quick).

Best wishes,

Alan

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] "cov.bases" in "tileMethylCounts"
messages.body_plain:
Dear Altuna,

Good day to you.

Let say if we set window size 1000bp, step size 1000 bp, cov bases=3, meaning output might contain 1000 bp with cov bases more than 3, in this case, can we know how many CpG site covered (covered bases) in each output of 1000 bp?

Thank you so much for your time.

Best wishes,
Wai Feng

On Friday, February 7, 2014 at 12:10:22 AM UTC+8, Altuna Akalin wrote:

> Hi Li,
> If there is no CpG covered in the window, a window will not be generated, but number of covered bases should be greater than or equal to "cov.bases". The default could have been 1 as well but it doesn't change anything, since there should be at least 1 CpG covered to create the window. Technically the window is created by discarded later on if it doesn't overlap with a covered base. Only after then cov.bases threshold is applied.
>
> covered >= cov.bases
>
>
> Best,
> Altuna
>

> On Thu, Feb 6, 2014 at 3:39 PM, <slee...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > Hi Altuna,
> >
> > I have a question regarding the "tileMethylCounts" function: According to the methylkit document, "cov.bases" is the minimum number of bases to be covered in a given window, and the default value is 0. When the value is 0, my understanding is that a window is generated even when it does not contain any sampled CpG, and thus the number of windows for each sample should be the same (as the number of windows in this case is only affected by the genome size). However, the actual numbers of windows generated in each samples are still slightly different when cov.bases=0. So I wondered what exactly does "cov.bases" mean? Does "cov.bases=0" require at least 1 sampled CpG in the window?
> >
> > Thank you very much!
> >
> > Best,
> > Li

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] "cov.bases" in "tileMethylCounts"
messages.body_plain:
This is calculated internally but not a part of the output object. To get the exact number of covered CpGs, you need to use countOverlaps or similar functionality from GenomicRanges with the input of your final tiles and original methlyKit object. You need to coerce methylKit objects to GRanges. In the vignette, we show how to do that

messages.subject: Errors in annotating DMRs in CHG context
messages.subject_clean: Errors in annotating DMRs in CHG context
messages.body_plain:
Dear groups members,

I encountered errors while annotating DMR,s in my data. Below are commands used from reading the sorted sam files to when I got the error message.

> CHGNL_list=list("NL0H.sam","NL42D.sam")
> CHGNL.methRaw=processBismarkAln(location=CHGNL_list,sample.id <http://sample.id>=list("NL0H","NL42D"),assembly = "Fragaria vesca 4.0.a1", save.folder=getwd(),save.context="CHG",read.context = "CHG",nolap=FALSE,mincov=10,minqual=20,phred64=FALSE,treatment=c(0,1))

> CHGNL.merge= unite(CHGNL.methRaw,destrand = FALSE)

> CHGNL.Diff=calculateDiffMeth(CHGNL.merge)

> CHGNL.Diff25p=getMethylDiff(CHGNL.Diff,difference=25,qvalue=0.01)
> CHGNLgene.obj=readTranscriptFeatures("/data2/Relindis_WGBS/WGBS_R_analysis/Fragaria_vesca_v4.0.a1.transcripts.Bed")
> DMCHGNL=annotateWithGeneParts(as(CHGNL_Diff25p,"GRanges"),CHGNLgene.obj)

Error in .get_data_frame_col_as_numeric(df, granges_cols[["start"]]) :
  some values in the "start" column cannot be turned into numeric values

I have previously and successfully used the same commands when analyzing CpG and CHH contexts of the same files (except for CpG where I set the destrand option to TRUE) and do not know what went wrong this time.

Any information to help me fix this error is highly appreciated.

Thank you.
